subject: Audit event schema and SSO exception for ClearSky POC
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Green <samantha@clearsky.io>; Charles Li <charles.li@clearsky.com>
Cc: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 22 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Audit event schema and SSO exception for ClearSky POC

Hi Samantha & Charles —

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Two ask items came out of the call that I wanted to capture so we can triage with Security/Product/Eng:

1) Audit events: ClearSky needs a consistent event stream for their POC (login, model_invoke, file_upload, policy_violation). They asked for a sample schema and whether we can include user_id, session_id, request_latency_ms, model_version.

2) SSO exemption: their IdP (legacy Okta tenant bound to a partner account) cannot be migrated in time for the POC start next week. They asked if we can grant a time-limited SSO "exemption" for a small set of test users while still capturing SSO-related events and enforcing 2FA.

I've attached a draft audit event spec and a proposed SSO exemption template to this thread for reference. Can Mina & Karthik weigh in on feasibility and any compliance blockers? Marcus, can you ballpark implementation effort for streaming those events from Priv deployments?

I want to keep this scoped as tight as possible for the POC: aim to provide event schema + a controlled exemption policy with logging and retention limits.

Thanks —
Vanessa
Director, Strategic Partnerships
Redwood Inference

Attachments: audit_event_spec_v1.pdf; sso_exemption_template.docx

From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Samantha Green <samantha@clearsky.io>
Date: Tue, 22 Mar 2027 13:05:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Audit event schema and SSO exception for ClearSky POC

Vanessa —

Quick read: the event schema looks reasonable as a starting point. A few compliance notes:

- For the exemption, we need an audit trail that ties any non-SSO auth to an approver and a documented time window (start/end).
- Retention: POC logs can be retained for 90 days by default; any longer retention requires Legal sign-off if events include PII.
- SOC2 evidence: if ClearSky requests SOC2-style evidence for the POC, we must ensure the exported logs are tamper-evident (signed/hashed) and we capture provenance (who approved exemptions).

I'll add a short checklist for the exemption template. Marcus — can you confirm whether the current Priv image can emit the required fields to our AuditStream endpoint, or do we need a small shim?

Cheers,
Mina
Head of Security Operations

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>, Samantha Green <samantha@clearsky.io>
Date: Wed, 23 Mar 2027 07:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Audit event schema and SSO exception for ClearSky POC

On Tue, Mar 22, 2027 at 9:12 AM Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai> wrote:
> 
> I want to keep this scoped as tight as possible for the POC: aim to provide event schema + a controlled exemption policy with logging and retention limits.

We can stream the fields as-is from Priv deployments. Implementation notes:

- Short term (POC): add a small adaptor in the Priv agent (1 engineer, ~3 days) to map local auth events to the audit schema and push to AuditStream. We will include user_id, session_id, timestamp, event_type, model_version, latency_ms.
- Exemption enforcement: we'll implement a flag that marks sessions as "exempted-auth" so Security can filter. The approver name & ticket id can be embedded in the event metadata.
- Export: create a signed daily bundle (SHA256 + metadata) that Mina can use for SOC2 evidence.

Risk: if the POC tenant enables heavy traffic, we'll need to throttle export frequency to control cost.

I'll prepare a short PR and a runbook for the POC – ETA: initial adaptor + runbook by Fri (Mar 26).

—Marcus

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>, Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Samantha Green <samantha@clearsky.io>
Date: Wed, 23 Mar 2027 11:18:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Audit event schema and SSO exception for ClearSky POC

Thanks — good alignment. A couple product/roadmap notes:

- We can treat this as a scoped "privops" feature for POC: 1) audit-event adaptor, 2) temporary exemption policy with an approval workflow, 3) signed export. That maps to a minimal deliverable we can ship quickly.
- Prioritization: I can slot this as a high-priority POC task but need sign-off from Compliance (Laura) on retention and allowed metadata.
- UX: recommend a small checkbox in the Priv Console to enable "SSO exemption mode for named users" and a modal to capture approver & ticket number. This keeps the UI friction low.

Laura — would you be able to confirm the 90-day retention allowed for POC logs? If not, what's the expected minimum for evidence exports?

I'll block an engineering sync for Thu morning to review the adaptor contract.

-Karthik
Senior PM, Platform

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Samantha Green <samantha@clearsky.io>, Charles Li <charles.li@clearsky.com>
Date: Thu, 24 Mar 2027 18:05:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Audit event schema and SSO exception for ClearSky POC

Folks —

90 days retention for POC logs is acceptable from a compliance perspective provided we redact or avoid storing any unnecessary PII fields (cleartext emails, SSNs, etc.). For the event schema, please ensure:

- user_id can be an internal opaque identifier (GUID) rather than an email address when possible;
- store an approver_id and ticket_ref for any exemption;
- export bundles are hashed and accompanied by a manifest with timestamps and an approver signature.

Samantha/Charles — we'll need a signed copy of the POC scope and a POA (point of access) list that contains the email addresses of test users who will be exempted. Please return that by EOD Mon so we can finalize the exemption template.

Next steps summary:
1) Marcus: adaptor + runbook by Fri (Mar 26)
2) Mina: finalize checklist for exemption template by Thu EOD
3) Karthik: host an engineering sync Thu morning (invite sent)
4) Samantha/Charles: provide signed POC scope + POA list by Mon EOD

If everyone is aligned I'll approve the limited exemption flow for the POC.

Thanks,
Laura
Head of Compliance, Redwood Inference
